outcome: Terms updated 24 July 2026 establish cohort-specific commitment periods; the legacy blanket rule for earlier customers is corrected.
Current 30GB JPY2,970/month remains valid through 2026-11-30; official ahamo materials schedule a tiered JPY3,135/40GB entry plan from 2026-12-01.
Current official support separates a 180-day chargeable-use rule from a 180-day top-up/plan credit rule; the old £5/180-day model is not safe to publish as a settled minimum.

CIN 1 remains documented at AZN3.99/30 days with one-way blocking after expiry if neither the fee nor a top-up is made, plus an AZN0.99/6-day extension option, but CIN 1 now appears in Bakcell’s tariff archive rather than the current GO tariff surface.

Users reported SIM in Safe disappearing from the app and remote re-activation failing after technical changes; support reportedly confirmed the service could still be attached even when not visible. Treat remote enablement/status visibility as a live operational risk.

Current policy establishes a 90-day no-transaction restriction followed by 275 days of office-restorable retention before termination. China roaming and international top-up are current for eligible prepaid lines, while the foreigner-specific Hello product is local-only and cannot be assumed equivalent to the roaming-capable ordinary prepaid route.

Current BH Telecom webshop material establishes the Ultra top-up validity ladder and a 150-day post-credit number-retention/recovery period; visitor eSIM products and foreign-issued-card top-ups are current.

BTC prepaid remains current and legacy prepaid plans were replaced in 2025, but current number lifecycle, minimum keep-alive action, foreigner acquisition and China-specific prepaid roaming remain unresolved.
The product and same-number extension path are current: 3GB annual entry is now ¥7,860 and the dedicated extension product is ¥5,400, with SMS reception and extension support explicitly listed.

Current Cellcard official surfaces conflict on the post-expiry top-up recovery window: the English business/self-service terms say expired balance can be restored by top-up within 30 calendar days, while the current Khmer main-site terms state 180 days. Do not infer number-retention/recycling timing from either balance-recovery window until reconciled.

Legacy GEL2/year was a rough estimate. Current official unit pricing and 90-day lifecycle imply a lower theoretical paid-action floor, but passive incoming SMS should not be relied on as the reset action.

The 180-day lifecycle is current and confirmed, but the legacy NT$100/NT$200-per-year floor was not re-established as the current minimum qualifying recharge. Preserve the lifecycle and leave the minimum cost unresolved.
Claro terms establish 180-day recharge validity plus a 60-day active grace period; current foreigner acquisition and prepaid roaming paths are also documented.
The legacy 90-day recharge and recycle timing could not be independently reverified against current 2026 Claro pages in this round. Preserve it only as a HOLD signal, not a current-guaranteed rule.

Current Claro Chile prepaid evidence establishes subscriber identification and a 180-day total recharge/recovery window, but current foreign-passport new-line activation, prepaid overseas SMS behavior and foreign-card recharge execution remain unresolved.

Current Claro Colombia prepaid evidence establishes a COP1,000 recharge floor, 60-day recharge validity, line-deactivation risk after 60 days without movements and free incoming roaming SMS in supported prepaid destinations; foreign-user initial registration and mainland-China coverage remain unresolved.

Current official FROG terms retain the number for up to 13 months from activation/last balance renewal, while the current electronic minimum top-up for FROG is EUR13; the legacy EUR10 keep-alive estimate is withdrawn.

Cricket 12-month Unlimited remains USD300 prepaid; unpaid service is suspended with a 60-day number-recovery boundary. Cricket Passport now includes China, while Wi-Fi Calling requires prior Cricket-network attachment and China-first acquisition/payment remain unresolved.

CTExcel UK and its Back to China SIM Retention Plan are current. Community evidence repeatedly reports a 90-day activity rule for some no-plan accounts but also plan-dependent retention and conflicting post-plan behavior. The provider-visible pages do not cleanly expose current retention eligibility, price and post-expiry mechanics, so no universal lifecycle or annual keep cost is asserted.

Current Cyta material resolves the legacy gap: EUR 5, 10, 20, 35 or 50 credit top-ups each grant 365 days; after the 365-day deadline outgoing service stops, followed by 7 days incoming-only and 15 additional days before number cancellation.
Legacy LKR500/365d was not found in the current official ladder. Current documented options are LKR400/180d and LKR1000/365d; exact additive stacking behavior remains a caveat.
Current CelcomDigi documentation directly confirms Digi RM100=120-day reload validity and an explicit RM198/365-day validity extension.

Current Digicel terms establish deactivation after four months with no usage and new-number assignment after reactivation; current visitor acquisition, international top-up and China roaming exist, but the exact clock-resetting keep-alive action is unresolved.

Current provider instructions resolve the legacy validity gap: three months from first activation, twelve months after every recharge, then a one-month expired window in which incoming calls/messages and recharging remain possible.

The old AED10-per-quarter framing is not needed for the current normalized rule. Current e& pages state lifetime validity with continued use and a 12-month retention/revival window after non-use; exact minimum annual cash cost is therefore left unresolved.

The €2/month plan remains current, but eligibility is expressly limited to people residing in metropolitan France or able to justify a stable link with metropolitan France; it is not a general non-resident acquisition route.
newly obtained number appeared associated with a prior Telegram account
multiple overseas users reported closures/suspensions and loss of service
some previously closed accounts/numbers were restored; not universal
multiple eventual refund successes observed after delays or earlier denials; outcome remains mixed

GO PAYG resets its inactivity clock with a top-up or chargeable event; 90 days without one enters a 275-day grace period, after which the SIM disconnects unless reactivated. Visitor eSIM can be obtained through the GO app before arrival and PAYG roaming is enabled on activation.
The legacy $20/180-day mechanism traces to old Petro-Canada-era evidence and is not supported by a current Good2Go provider rule in this audit; post-network-transition structure remains unresolved.

Flexible remains USD20/month + USD10/GB, China is in the international destination list with free texts, but Fi requires a valid U.S. payments address and at least one day of U.S. activation/use before international service; extended overseas data remains restricted.

Legacy BDT995/5-year claim is stale. Current first-party surfaces show approximately BDT1497-1498 for five-year account validity, with a BDT1 discrepancy between official pages. Keep BDT300/365-day recharge as the clean current floor until the five-year price conflict is reconciled.

Current Israeli recharge retailers consistently advertise a HOTALK 66 ILS pay-per-use balance load with 180-day validity, but current first-party evidence tying that balance validity to the phone-number deactivation/recycling lifecycle was not located. The legacy no-KYC claim is also withdrawn as unverified.

Current PAYG legal terms permit disconnection after four months without credit, a bundle or a chargeable event and expire unused credit after 365 days without an additional top-up. Current iD marketing/community wording also says 180 days, so the conflict is preserved rather than silently choosing the looser interval.
Current IF Mobile pricing remains available, but the prior remote image-plus-selfie identity flow ended 2026-03-31; current nonresident remote signup and mainland-China SMS utility remain unresolved.
Current provider evidence confirms JPY850/month 2GB voice pricing, Japan-address/identity/payment gating, and overseas voice/SMS availability for voice SIM/eSIM.

Current Jazz material resolves foreigner purchase requirements and prepaid roaming/incoming-SMS pricing, but SIM Lagao is only a 60-day reactivation promotion and does not establish final number-lifecycle or minimum keep-alive economics.

kölbi terms tie 90 days without a chargeable main-balance event or recharge to definitive liquidation and number disposal; current tourist/passport acquisition and China roaming make the route usable as backstage evidence without inventing a cheapest annual cost.

KT now provides an exact recharge-validity ladder up to KRW50,000/365 days, but passport-only usage is short-term/90-day constrained without further identity verification and Welcome Prepaid excludes roaming.
The 274-day active plus 91-day suspension rule and UAH30 restoration threshold are supported by current operator material and 2026 enforcement reporting.
Current LABAS rules directly confirm the €3/90-day account rule and 120-day hard number-loss boundary.

Lebara France currently runs on SFR. Top-ups from EUR5 are described as valid for 90 days, but contract summaries separately permit termination after 90 consecutive days without service use; the legacy EUR15/90-day top-up-only retention claim is withdrawn.
inbound verification SMS worked while outgoing SMS/voice/Wi-Fi Calling were initially incomplete or conflicting

Current LG U+ first-party evidence resolves a visitor SIM with a 010 number, while a separate LG U+ network MVNO (U+ UMobile) carries the long-term prepaid product. The legacy route identity is therefore not safely attributable to one current product, and the MVNO prepaid plans list roaming as unavailable.

Current LINEMO pricing, resident-foreigner identity requirements, contract fee and overseas SMS mechanics are documented; new-number lines cannot enroll in World Support until the fifth billing month.
LMT confirms a 60-day advance-validity plus 60-day receive-only structure and a €1 online refill minimum, but the old €3 every 60 days / €18-year model does not follow from the current pages.

The 120-day / £15 annual keep-number mechanism has fresh independent corroboration, and the legacy O2 host-network field is stale: current UK service runs on EE. The UK first-party FAQ text was not retrievable in this audit.
Independent 2026 reports confirm the AT&T migration and include service/account/SIM-swap failures during transition. These are incident evidence, not a route-wide failure rate.

Current official terms retain the 60-day non-use expiry. A current 12-month 8 GB plan is USD 108, so the old USD 120/year claim is not a valid minimum-retention fact; exact PAYG keep-alive cost remains unresolved.
Provider charges 1 GEL at service activation on a new number and the next 1 GEL on day 181. Treat ~2.03 GEL/year as the annualized 180-day run-rate, not an exact first-year cash-total guarantee.

Current JAWAL terms establish a 12-month card validity renewed by each recharge, SIM/eSIM support and identity-backed activation. Recent visitor-eSIM reports preserve real tourist acquisition plus fulfillment friction; foreign-passport long-term eligibility is not inferred from generic identity-document language.

Current Mint terms establish suspension at plan expiry and cancellation/reassignment risk after 60 days without successful renewal while suspended. The 12-month 6GB plan remains USD180/year. Official Wi-Fi Calling is usable abroad, while reliable China-first activation/payment and standalone China cellular SMS/OTP remain unresolved.

Tourist prepaid acquisition explicitly accepts a foreign passport, but the Number Retention page says outlet enrollment or a letter enclosing NIC. Foreign-passport holder retention enrollment, especially remotely, remains unresolved.

Current prepaid contract ties recharge to active service and permits cancellation after seven months without recharge; current foreign-national acquisition is in-person/biometric, while prepaid-specific overseas SMS and China behavior remain unresolved.

MTN Number For Life provides 12- or 24-month prepaid number reservation and current prepaid roaming supports SMS, but MTN-specific foreign-user registration guidance conflicts with the regulator’s foreign-prepaid path.

Current MTN prices are NGN3,500/1 year, NGN5,000/2 years and NGN7,500/3 years. Current prepaid terms also establish a visitor registration path without NIN for stays under 24 months, subject to valid visa and passport/travel documentation.

MTS Belarus withdraws a number after 60 days without top-up following forced blocking, or after 180 days with a positive balance but no operations; however the current guest tariff explicitly disables roaming and SMS roaming for foreign citizens/stateless persons.

MTS support updated in 2026 confirms the Сохраняю номер service exists for eligible no-monthly-fee tariffs and that most lines face termination after roughly six months without qualifying top-up or spend. The product-price page remains geo-fragile, so tariff eligibility should stay constrained.
Ncell now documents both the visitor acquisition path and the long-duration prepaid recharge-validity ladder; China roaming is current, while application-specific OTP behavior remains unverified.

A 300–499 CZK top-up gives only six months of credit validity, but O2 separately states the prepaid SIM/card itself remains valid for 12 months from the last top-up. Do not confuse credit expiry with number/SIM expiry.

Current Omantel agreement establishes 90-day prepaid validity plus a 90-day number-holding period; current Hayyak supports passport eSIM acquisition, card/app recharge and free incoming SMS while roaming.

Current provider pages establish a 90-day active window, EUR2 online top-up floor and an extended tourist-eSIM recharge grace period, while roaming terms explicitly exclude Tourist Package users from roaming outside Montenegro.

Current One NZ terms make Prepay credit expire 360 days after top-up and the service inactive with number loss if no new credit is added. Minimum logged-in website/app top-up is NZD10. Physical Prepay activation requires One NZ mobile coverage; China is a current Prepay roaming destination, while service-specific OTP reliability is not guaranteed.

Current Hala evidence establishes a QAR10 minimum recharge, 30-day active credit validity followed by 179 days of grace before line deactivation, passport/QID verification and current prepaid roaming coverage including China; OTP reliability remains unverified.

Legacy A$59/186-day and A$180/365-day retention economics are stale. Current official long-expiry options are A$180/186 days and A$350/365 days, while Optus states the 365-day A$350 price rises to A$395 on 2026-09-30.

Current Orange rules confirm the active/grace ladder and show the legacy €42/year estimate was not defensible: a €5 recharge grants 30 active days plus 300 grace days, while grace can receive calls/SMS.

The previously unresolved fee is now explicit: XOF 3,000/6 months, XOF 5,000/12 months and XOF 10,000/24 months. Subscription is available via airtime USSD or Orange Money, and the extension starts on the subscription date.

Current Proximus pages say Pay&Go is valid 12 months after first call and >EUR5 top-up extends 12 months, but the current FAQ separately says a card not used for more than 6 months is automatically deactivated. The reviewed page does not define exactly which activity satisfies “used”; annual top-up alone must not be treated as sufficient.

Current Rakuten pricing and overseas service are documented, while foreign-customer onboarding remains a Japanese-residence-document path and Rakuten Link should be initialized in Japan before travel.
The annual product remains current, but the legacy $60/$30 economics are stale. Current Essentials is $80 first year and renews at $110/year; activation must occur in the United States.

Daima pricing remains directly documented on Safaricom pages: KSh200/6 months, KSh500/1 year and KSh1000/2 years. The product pages are older, so continued live availability remains a monitoring item.
Current SK Telecom material establishes the PPS recharge lifecycle, passport onboarding and stay-expiry recharge constraint; current roaming guidance classifies PPS as roaming-unavailable.

Smart ordinary prepaid lifecycle remains 365 days for loaded value plus a 180-day reload grace after balance reaches zero, but foreign tourists face a separate 30-day SIM-registration validity cap unless an approved visa extension is supplied. The legacy route is therefore not treated as a generally available long-term foreign-user route.

Current SMARTY material resolves the old monthly-payment-only assumption: a plan can remain inactive before automatic account closure at 220 days, while current China roaming explicitly lists free incoming SMS; active service must be renewed before relying on calls/text/data.

Current StarHub Prepaid is a monthly-plan product with a 120-day post-expiry grace period. Passport-only prepaid registration is limited to 30 days unless re-registered using an eligible Singapore-issued identity/work pass; the legacy cheap-USSD/top-up retention model is withdrawn.

Current STC personal prepaid terms document 180-day SIM validity from paid activity, while a still-live STC recharge page says 360 days; non-citizen final-departure/ID-expiry cancellation remains a structural blocker.

Historical Talkmobile PAYG ended on 31 August 2017; current Talkmobile sells contract/SIM-only plans only, so the PAYG route remains preserved as discontinued negative knowledge rather than remapped to a current subscription.
Current Telekom rules replace the legacy recurring 90-day assumption: the first top-up is due within 90 days of activation, then each top-up extends the SIM and nominal credit by 180 days.

Current Free2Go material establishes active acquisition, a EUR 5 recharge floor and the 90/180/270-day lifecycle; general prepaid terms allow SIM disconnection after day 270, while China OTP remains unverified.

Current Telenor Kontant uses a 12-month clock from the last recharge, followed by a two-month automatic reopening window. Current self-service access requires Telenor ID/BankID and web recharge cards are limited to Nordic-issued cards, so nonresident acquisition and maintenance remain constrained.

Current Telenor support confirms registered prepaid numbers and destination-specific prepaid roaming, while current purchase/recharge economics and foreign-user registration remain unresolved; legacy cheap annual pricing is withdrawn.
The legacy Telia DK prepaid label now conflicts with the current Norlys Mobil consumer surface; no current Telia-branded prepaid product/lifecycle was located, so the route remains HOLD.
Current Super guidance directly confirms the 180-day validity rule, EUR3 single-top-up threshold, 30-day receive-only recovery window, and eSIM starter availability.

Legacy Rp5,000/year keep-cost inference is unsupported by current rules. Rp5,000 top-up is not documented as a 365-day extension; official extension options include Rp115,000/360 days, while qualifying usage/top-up/package rules may yield cheaper paths whose durable annual minimum remains unresolved.

Legacy 4p-text / GBP0.08-year keep estimate belonged to retired PAYG pricing. Current Essentials standard SMS is 10p, so a two-actions-per-year theoretical floor is about GBP0.20 after the required initial top-up.

Tigo Tanzania is now Yas Tanzania with core services/contracts continued; current Yas terms allow suspension/re-allocation after 90 days non-use and current roaming lists China, while TCRA visitor registration is limited to visitors staying no more than four months.

Connect remains USD15/month for 5GB. Current prepaid support allows cancellation and number loss after more than 120 days in Not Paid status. Current prepaid roaming publishes USD0.10 incoming SMS outside Canada, includes China in the country table and provides no prepaid data roaming.

The legacy THB35/90d and THB70/180d validity-extension mechanism remains useful community intelligence, but current 2026 first-party terms were not reachable. Keep the row as HOLD and do not present the price as current-guaranteed.
Light remains USD 10 monthly or USD 96/year. Native roaming cannot work until the line has domestic U.S. usage; Warp/Dark Star Wi-Fi Calling setup also requires U.S. coverage.
Legacy GS2 pricing was community-only; the current VinaPhone GS2 product page directly supports VND120,000 for a 360-day validity extension.

Visible base remains USD25/month or USD275/year. Current terms suspend nonpayment-deactivated service for 60 days before cancellation/reassignment. Official Wi-Fi Calling works internationally when enabled before leaving the U.S.; current independent evidence corroborates long-duration use abroad, while overseas first activation remains contradictory.

Legacy 83-day inactivity and 100-day recycle summary is not the current first-party rule. Current Vodacom prepaid terms say suspension/disconnection may occur after service has not been used for more than 110 days. Exact final recycle timing remains unresolved.

Vodafone Egypt prepaid foreigner KYC and prepaid roaming are current, but Park Your Line is explicitly a postpaid service and Tourist Line is a separate visitor product; neither establishes generic prepaid long-term number retention.

Current Vodafone NL prepaid keeps credit and number active with at least one paid call, SMS, mobile-data session or top-up every six months; after six months of inactivity there is a three-month frozen-credit recovery window. Current community evidence shows overseas acquisition/payment variability and successful SMS/OTP reception, while China-specific cellular OTP reliability remains evidence-scoped.

The legacy route ID/brand refers to Vodafone TUTI. The current provider surface is One Hungary and the active product is Tuti Feltöltőkártya. Preserve the legacy ID for comparison continuity but use the current One/Tuti product identity.
Current Yettel material resolves SIM validity and online top-up, but the available digital-registration instructions document selfie plus ID-card capture rather than a verified foreign-passport path.
Yettel explicitly says top-up sent from another Yettel prepaid/postpaid number does not prolong card expiry. Use a standard top-up channel for lifecycle renewal.

Current eeZee supports a KD13 365-day validity extension, KD5 new prepaid voice line, expatriate passport/Civil-ID purchase, eSIM, remote recharge and prepaid voice/SMS roaming by default; China-specific OTP remains unverified.
